title: Prior art: Birkhoff's connection matrix for $q$-difference systems, and its hypothesis
html:
Birkhoff studies systems Y(qx) = Q(x)\, Y(x) with |q| > 1 and Q a matrix of polynomials of degree at most \mu [birkhoff1913, \S 18, eq. (54), p. 559]. He restricts to the case in which there are matrix solutions Y_0 at x = 0 and Y_\infty at x = \infty of a prescribed form, built from series analytic at the respective point whose leading coefficients have non-zero determinant; only that case is considered [birkhoff1913, \S 18, p. 561]. The connection matrix P, defined by Y_0(x) = Y_\infty(x)\, P(x), is analytic away from 0 and \infty and satisfies P(qx) = P(x) [birkhoff1913, \S 18, p. 561]. Counting the constants in Y_0, Y_\infty and P that survive the freedom to rescale columns, he finds n^2\mu + 1 characteristic constants, the same number as the invariants of the system, and proves that a system can be constructed with any assigned set of them, up to integer shifts of some exponents [birkhoff1913, \S\S 20--21, pp. 565--566].

This is the original source for the connection matrix between 0 and \infty that the kernel conjecture refers to, and its convention |q| > 1 is the one the corpus uses for the substrate parameter.

It does not cover the corpus's carrier. The module \mathcal{K} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at infinity, so its formal solutions there need the ramified variable x^{1/2} and are not of the form Birkhoff assumes. His existence and counting results therefore do not apply to \mathcal{K} as stated, and citing them does not reopen a route that depends on that hypothesis.
